clue.text: Lack of resources to install secretary in Cuzco?

indicators.note: to install something is to set it inside, so the secretary goes into the city

parts.note: Cuzco was the capital of the Inca empire, an Inca city; the question mark flags the example
a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a lack of funds stops a secretary being installed in a Peruvian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapacity is inability or lack of means, so a lack of resources describes it loosely.

clue.text: Some cows caught by the ears

indicators.note: something caught by the ears is picked up through hearing, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: caught, of a sound, means heard

explanation.surface: A few cows are grabbed by their ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a group of cattle, so some cows together make one.

clue.text: Vehicle carries a small weight

indicators.note: the vehicle carries the letter inside itself, so it is placed within

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: A vehicle is loaded with a light load.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a unit of weight for gems, a fifth of a gram.

clue.text: Invisible speaker in weakness getting nothing finished

indicators.note: the weakness gets the nothing put inside it, so one goes within the other

parts.note: a vice is a moral weakness
O looks like zero, nothing
over means finished

explanation.surface: An unseen speaker, in a weak moment, gets nothing done.
explanation.definitionFit: A voiceover is narration by a speaker who is not seen on screen.

clue.text: No justice, unable to move for this?

parts.note: no is a negative answer
equity is fairness, justice

explanation.surface: Someone complains of no justice and being stuck because of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Homeowners whose mortgage exceeds the house's value cannot sell up and move, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing more on a mortgage than the property is worth traps owners, who cannot afford to sell and relocate.

clue.text: Star workers are arrested

indicators.note: the workers have arrested, or held, the word are within them

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Celebrity employees are taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is a bright red star in the constellation Scorpius.

clue.text: If impostor, celebrate victory

definitions.meaning: in Kipling's poem If, ... and disaster are called two impostors

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's If says 'If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster / And treat those two impostors just the same', so the first definition is a literary allusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumph as a verb means exult, as a noun a victory, and Kipling calls it an impostor.

clue.text: Pupil who shouldn't grow up to be a lady of the night?

definitions.text: Pupil who shouldn't grow up to be a lady of the night?

parts.words: Pupil who shouldn't grow up to be a lady of the night?
parts.note: a schoolgirl who goes home each evening rather than boarding is, by name, the opposite of a woman of the night

explanation.walkthrough: A school pupil who does not board is a day pupil; the joke sets her against a 'lady of the night', a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl attending a boarding school by day only, going home at night, is so called.

clue.text: In spree, put down pounds for kitchen equipment

indicators.note: the pounds go in the spree, placed inside it
put down means written or set down, here set within the word

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: During a shopping binge, someone pays out pounds on kitchen gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender is a kitchen appliance for liquidising food.

clue.text: Stan's 1500 metres?

parts.note: the name Stan sits at the centre of the word distance, so it is that word's middle

explanation.surface: A question about whether Stan ran the 1500 metres.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1500 metres is a classic middle-distance race in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: Races from 800 to 1500 metres are classed as middle distance events in athletics.

clue.text: Peevish when pencil set is damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grows irritable because their set of pencils is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Splenetic means bad-tempered or spiteful, the spleen being the old seat of ill humour.

clue.text: Secret request dropped by learner

indicators.note: the request is dropped, or let go of, by the learner word, so it is removed

parts.note: a beginner is a learner
to beg is to request

explanation.surface: A secret request is abandoned by a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones, kept hidden or secret.

clue.text: Be hanged, maybe, at end of gibbet, and cut down

parts.note: being hanged is one way to die

indicators.note: the end of the word gibbet supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: A condemned man is hanged at the gallows and then taken down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'cut down' as taking a body from the gibbet; it means reduce, as in eating less.
explanation.definitionFit: To diet is to cut down on food, reducing intake to lose weight.

clue.text: Only pearls work for me

indicators.note: work as in working dough, so the letters are kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says only pearls will do for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something applies personally means it applies to me myself, speaking for myself.

clue.text: Head off little chap, a minor irritant

indicators.note: taking the head off means losing the first letter

parts.note: titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A small boy is told to go away because he is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is informal British for a small person, often a child.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a small irritation of the skin, minor but annoying.

clue.text: Joining work, bear to get shut inside

indicators.note: the word for shut goes inside the word for bear

parts.note: to bear is to carry
pent means shut up or confined, as in pent-up

explanation.surface: A bear is locked inside while carpentry is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry involves joinery, making wooden joints, so it is joining work.

clue.text: Christian home: mine has acres, in which dog lives

indicators.note: the dog lives in the mine and acres, so it goes inside them
lives means dwells within, placing one piece inside another

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
has can be is, as in the old 'he is come'
acres are land
a cairn is a small Scottish terrier

explanation.surface: A Christian household's mine includes land where the dog stays.
explanation.walkthrough: Fletcher Christian led the Bounty mutineers, who settled on this Pacific island, so 'Christian' is a man, not a believer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bounty mutineer Fletcher Christian made his home on this remote Pacific island.

clue.text: Non-uniform riddle heard that is close to libellous

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the word sounds like what is written

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A puzzle is overheard that seems almost defamatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Civvies are civilian clothes, worn by soldiers out of uniform.

clue.text: With explosive packed round, trip weapon

indicators.note: the explosive is packed round the trip, enclosing it

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
a ride is a trip

explanation.surface: A journey is booby-trapped with explosives as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, a weapon of Neptune and gladiators.

clue.text: Postscript shows unattractive emotion — cut both bits

indicators.note: a cut word loses its end, here its last letter

parts.note: envy is an ugly feeling
binary bits are 0 and 1, which look like O and I

explanation.surface: A postscript reveals jealousy, but both parts are trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is a short closing stanza or postscript to a poem or book.

clue.text: In peak area race a sort of horse

parts.note: the Derby is a famous flat horse race at Epsom
a shire is a large draught horse

explanation.surface: A horse race in the hills features a heavy horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peak District national park lies mostly in this English county; lower-case 'peak' hides the proper name.
explanation.definitionFit: Derbyshire contains most of the Peak District, so it is the Peak area.

clue.text: Overlong joke splitting sides, Alan beginning to explode uncontrollably

indicators.note: the joke splits the other letters by sitting inside them
letters out of control scatter into a new order
the beginning of explode is its first letter

parts.note: a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: A long-winded joke has Alan splitting his sides and laughing uncontrollably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting sides' tempts a laughing joke, but 'sides' is anagram fodder; 'uncontrollably' mixes the pool to SESEDALIAN, and 'splitting' places the joke after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesquipedalian means using long words, literally a foot and a half long.

clue.text: Made aimless nomads ride off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Wandering nomads set off on a ride without purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Randomised means arranged by chance, without aim or pattern.

clue.text: Health-giving food needs cuttin' up to be swallowed

indicators.note: the chopping is swallowed by the food, going inside it

parts.note: a meal is food
cutting up is dicing; the dropped g leaves dicin'

explanation.surface: Healthy food has to be chopped up before eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal means having healing properties, so health-giving.

clue.text: Rowdy youngster given notice in brief communication

indicators.note: the notice goes in the shortened communication
brief means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a letter is a written communication
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A loud teenager is given a short note of warning.
explanation.walkthrough: A LADETTE is British slang for a young woman behaving boisterously, drinking hard like the lads.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman with loud, boozy, laddish behaviour.

clue.text: Cuts faction in again

indicators.note: the faction goes in the word for again

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used for an encore or repeat
a sect is a faction

explanation.surface: A group divides again.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two halves, so it cuts.

clue.text: Go deeply inside model — very deficient

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Go deep into a model that is lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very deficient' adds to the surface: the hidden run stops short of the whole of 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig or probe deeply into something.

clue.text: Play given run in old city

indicators.note: the run goes in the word for play

parts.note: to toy is to play
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A drama given a run in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city besieged by the Greeks in Homer.
